headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error: Kestra can write/egress broadly while Perplexity is vendor-hosted with browser-based retrieval, creating default pathways for sensitive workflow data to leave the host and be reused without verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can write workflow artifacts and logs to shared files, and B can ingest uploaded documents and browsing context. That creates a plausible prompt-injection bridge if A-generated content is fed into B, even though no explicit shared channel is documented. Because the pathway exists in default-ish file-based workflows, medium is warranted.
conditions: IF A writes untrusted text into files that B later uploads or reads
IF B treats uploaded documents or browsing context as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Separate A output folders from any B upload folder
Strip instructions from A-generated artifacts before upload
Use a human review step before B consumes A outputs
Mark A outputs as data-only in filenames and headers
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between A and B

B_data_leakage.rationale: A has broad network egress and reads/writes filesystem data including logs, database data, cloud storage data, and messages. B is vendor-hosted and analyzes uploaded PDFs/images plus browsing context, so sensitive A outputs can leave the host when passed to B. This is a default-dangerous leakage path with potentially irreversible exfiltration.
conditions: IF A outputs contain logs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, or notifications
IF those outputs are uploaded into B or pasted into B's browsing context
mitigations: Do not send sensitive A artifacts to B
Redact logs and database fields before any upload
Use synthetic samples for B analysis
Restrict A to non-sensitive datasets for paired runs
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on A-to-B handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; B cannot write the host filesystem but does maintain per-Space shared context across sessions. The main conflict is not direct write-write collision, but A can mutate shared artifacts while B reuses session context, creating overlapping mutable state without locking. Uncertainty about the exact bridge pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF A and B operate on the same shared workspace or uploaded artifact set
IF B reuses Space context across sessions for the same user
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces per agent
Freeze shared artifacts before B reads them
Avoid concurrent runs on the same files
Use timestamped copies instead of in-place edits
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can generate workflow outputs, logs, and notifications, while B is a search/RAG agent that can incorporate browsing context and citations. If B consumes A's outputs as authoritative without verification, A's mistakes can cascade into B's answers or actions. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B uses A-produced text as source material without independent verification
IF A-generated workflow outputs are forwarded into B's browsing or answer context
mitigations: Require B to cite primary sources, not A summaries
Add a verification checklist before B publishes outputs
Limit A outputs to machine-readable facts only
Flag A-originated content in B prompts
requires-engineering: implement source provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: A touches database, cloud storage, messages, and notifications, while B is vendor-hosted and processes uploaded documents and browsing context under its own privacy policy. That creates a plausible retention/residency mismatch for regulated data classes, especially if A's outputs include personal or sensitive records. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction breach, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated personal data from A is uploaded to B
IF B retention or residency terms differ from A's governance requirements
mitigations: Exclude regulated records from B inputs
Review B privacy terms before any upload
Use de-identified excerpts only
Keep an audit log of every A-to-B transfer
requires-engineering: formalize a data-processing agreement
